claims.text: Greg Short asserts that seeking a prescribed formula for success is incompatible with reaching the top tier; people who require someone else's step-by-step prescription end up looking up at those who did not, because top performers develop their path through direct experience rather than following others' frameworks.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
claims.speaker_term: somebody's prescription on how to be successful
conditions: Applies to entrepreneurial success contexts where individual agency and market feedback are the primary learning mechanism
claims.mechanism: Relying on prescribed frameworks shifts the practitioner into a consumer role rather than a builder role, limiting the direct-feedback loop that produces real competitive insight.
bounded_by: Speaker does not specify whether this applies to narrow technical skills requiring credentialed instruction

practices.text: Stop looking for somebody's prescription on how to be successful; develop your own path through direct experience rather than textbooks or consulting frameworks.
